req_desc:
Account-to-victory journey.
Provide the arrival journey through practice, account return, encounter selection and an accepted victory with exact identity, frame and progress read-back.

Durable identity.
Persist isolated accounts and revocable sessions with authoritative uniqueness and authentication.

Unranked tutorial.
Provide guided local practice that cannot create verified progress.

Inspectable rules.
Expose every simulation, arithmetic, randomness, ranking and limit rule through the Rules reference and API.

Campaign gates.
Derive ordered encounter completion and unlocks exclusively from accepted campaign victories.

Bound tickets.
Bind issued tickets immutably to their owner, definition, seed, loadout, source revision and ruleset.

Conserved defence journey.
Support the complete forecast, deployment, upgrade and salvage journey with exact frame and ledger reconciliation.

Deterministic frames.
Produce every frame through the published integer tick rules, including simultaneous attacks, deaths and breaches.

Charge transfers.
Persist balanced append-only transfers and balances for the independently reproduced legal command prefix.

Command legality.
Reject the first illegal command without trusting claims, sorting commands or repairing evidence.

Lantern Cast agreement.
Compare two spatial deployment forecasts from one frozen state and match subsequent command-free simulation.

Installation lifecycle.
Apply the documented upgrade, cooldown, salvage and installation-identity rules.

Verification recovery journey.
Support interrupted submission, identical replay, illegal evidence and later account return with exact result and derived-state read-back.

Independent acceptance.
Accept a result only after confirmed immutable evidence is read and independently reproduced by the server.

Submission ownership.
Give each ticket one canonical evidence submission and one terminal result under retries and concurrency.

Persistent return.
Restore verified completions, unlocks and result details after sign-out and sign-in.

Accepted effects.
Commit accepted metrics and qualifying progress or ranking effects together.

Revision-and-proof journey.
Support private editing, saved-revision playtesting and revision changes with exact definition, proof and frame read-back.

Private revisions.
Isolate private records and guard edits and proof associations by their saved revision.

Bounded work.
Enforce the published inclusive input and simulation bounds before expensive processing.

Proof qualification.
Expose proof states and qualify only a matching accepted winning demonstration.

Publication recovery journey.
Support proof-backed publication, interruption recovery and withdrawal with exact public and private read-back.

Complete publication.
Expose playable challenges only after required immutable objects and the authoritative publication commit exist.

Discovery-to-ranking journey.
Support indexed discovery and an original-rules attempt ending in exact ticket, result and board read-back.

Indexed discovery.
Search published challenges through Meilisearch with typed filters, truthful indexing state and recovery without restart.

Immutable public history.
Preserve published definitions and eligible historical results while applying the documented withdrawal visibility rules.

Season comparison journey.
Support multi-account comparison across the season boundary with exact ranks, percentages, daily challenge and streak read-back.

Derived rankings.
Derive ranks, personal best, completion counts and crew percentages from the same qualifying accepted results.

Shared study journey.
Support replay presentation and inspection across app processes with exact snapshot and frame read-back.

Evidence playback.
Reconstruct eligible replay and accepted frames from confirmed immutable objects under the documented access rules.

Keyboard completeness.
Implement the roving board, layered dialogs, shortcuts and focus preservation defined in Business rules.

Responsive touch layout.
Implement the reference viewport orders, contained table scrolling and explicit touch confirmation.

Observable motion.
Implement the forecast phases, meaningful feedback and immediate reduced-motion substitutes.

Harbour visual identity.
Present the specified materials, silhouettes, typography and restricted amber signals.

Announced feedback.
Show the documented pending, success, invalid, stale and unavailable states through the named live regions.

Dependency recovery.
Preserve authoritative state and the documented retry behavior through database, evidence and discovery failures.

Runtime and boundary.
Supply the deployment, initialization, configuration and same-origin boundary contracts.

Provider and simulation integrity.
Use real providers, explicit service configuration and one shared pure simulation implementation.

Live snapshots.
Follow database-backed replay presentation and leaderboard changes across processes while preserving inspector identity and focus.

Exact value presentation.
Preserve integer API and storage values while converting charge, percentages and editable game times exactly.

Season surfaces.
Present the season day, local time, daily challenge, standings and authenticated player's streak.

Season computation.
Compute every season surface from the same offset-aware day and ticket-bound daily selection.

Published transitions.
Enforce the run, challenge and proof transition tables, including system-only and nonpublic states.

Reviewable source.
Meet the explicit TypeScript engineering standards without duplicate ranking or transition decisions.

Spatial forecast composition.
Make the paired traces, contact marks, placement silhouette and charge comparison legible together over the actual pier.
Supply the working run manifest defined in Deployment.
Include THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md listing shipped packages and bundled font licences; shipped packages means the production dependency tree reported by npm ls --omit=dev --all --json.
Use only MIT, ISC, BSD-2-Clause, BSD-3-Clause or Apache-2.0 licences for shipped packages, SIL OFL-1.1 for bundled fonts and original procedural artwork.
Use only PostgreSQL, MinIO and Meilisearch as persistent services, without fallback datastores or fabricated provider success.
Preserve supplied service and evaluation configuration and do not use observer credentials.
